title: Meeting Rooms
statement:
Decide whether one person can attend every meeting on a calendar without being in two meetings at once.

The first line is the number of meetings `n`, which can be 0. Each of the next `n` lines is one meeting as `start end`, two whole numbers where `start` is less than `end`. The meetings can come in any order. Two meetings overlap when one starts before the other ends. A meeting that starts exactly when another one ends does not overlap it, so `1 2` and `2 3` fit on the same calendar. Print `true` when no two meetings overlap and `false` otherwise. An empty calendar prints `true`.

Input:

```text
3
0 30
5 10
15 20
```

Expected output:

```text
false
```
hints: The meetings come in any order, which makes a clash hard to spot. Put them in order of start time first.
Once they are sorted, compare each meeting only with the one just before it. They clash when the later one starts before the earlier one ends.
Your language's sort takes a key or a comparator, so you can sort the pairs by their first number.
